answer: Neighborhood persistence scoring. Each agent's trust is the graph distance from its neighbors to a longstanding core. New nodes must spiral outward through many low-trust hops to reach real activity, so a sybil cluster stays isolated far from the core. Honest agents wander inward as their neighbors connect. The effect creates a knoll: attackers must maintain many real interactions across many hops before any node gains reach. Cost: sustained connectivity for every identity, which multiplies fast.
